reasons.claim: The update channel was hijacked via a hosting-provider compromise from about June to Dec 2025, with targeted malware delivery, and was later hardened. In 2026 there were many further CVEs, including code-execution and installer issues in 8.9.x, and the repository has no SECURITY.md. The disclosure and fixes were reasonably transparent and fast, but the incident is recent and the patch cadence is high [E1, E2, E5, E7].
reasons.quote: Vulnerability in Notepad++

reasons.claim: The project depends on one lead maintainer, Don Ho, with community contributors. It has run since 2003 with continuous releases, but the bus factor and single point of failure remain, now combined with a recent supply-chain compromise [E3, E4].
reasons.quote: Notepad++ release 8.9.8 ... @donho donho released this 23 Aug

reasons.claim: There is no corporate legal entity or contractual vendor. Lookalike and impersonation sites are common, so downloads must come only from the official domain or GitHub [E10].
reasons.quote: notepad plus plus wants your help in parasite website shutdown

reasons.claim: There is no SLA, vendor support or formal certification. Code-signing lapsed in 2025 before being restored in 8.8.7. Enterprises should pin versions, deploy through managed channels, and manage the auto-updater [E6, E8].
reasons.quote: Notepad++ v8.8.3 - Self-signed Certificate: Certified by Code, Not Corporations

reasons.claim: No regulatory action or lawsuit against the project was found. The only item is a May 2026 trademark dispute over an unofficial macOS port, which ended in a rename [E9].
reasons.quote: Notepad++ Mac Port Renamed Nextpad++ After Trademark Row

reasons.claim: A single maintainer combined with a supply-chain compromise that ended less than a year ago is a bus-factor and single-point-of-failure risk, even though it was well handled.
reasons.quote: How state-sponsored attackers hijacked Notepad++ updates
